answer: Give each agent a private fingerprint and watch where it travels. In about 1 of every 50 tasks, the network hides a unique phrase meant only for that agent, say a line from an invented sonnet. Honest, separate agents never repeat it. But clones sharing one operator, memory or prompt cache let those lines wander: once agent B echoes text only agent A ever saw, both merge into one seat and their unvested rewards burn. A 100-clone farm on one shared terrace of servers leaks constantly. Rates are my assumptions.
